RELIANCE RANCHES, LLC AND CHANAS RANCH, LLC’S OBJECTIONS TO AND
MOTION TO STRIKE PORTIONS OF SAMUEL HV ABELL ON BEHALF OF ABELL
                RANCHES, LTD.’s DIRECT TESTIMONY

    COME NOW Intervenors Reliance Ranches, LLC (“Reliance Ranches”) and Chanas Ranch,

LLC (“Chanas Ranch”) and submit these objections and motion to strike portions of the direct

testimony filed by Samuel HV Abell on behalf of Abell Ranches, LTD. - Item 4160.

                                     I.     BACKGROUND

    Under the procedural schedule adopted for this proceeding, May 18, 2026, is the deadline for

Objection to Intervenor Direct Testimony. Accordingly, these objections and motion to strike are

timely filed.




RELIANCE RANCHES, LLC AND CHANAS RANCH, LLC’S OBJECTIONS TO AND MOTION TO STRIKE
PORTIONS OF SAMUEL HV ABELL ON BEHALF OF ABELL RANCHES, LTD.’S DIRECT TESTIMONY

(493,408)                                                                             PAGE 1 OF 8
         II.    OBJECTION TO AND MOTION TO STRIKE PORTIONS OF DIRECT
              TESTIMONY FILED BY SAMUEL HV ABELL ON BEHALF OF ABELL
                              RANCHES, LTD. - ITEM 4160

    Reliance Ranches and Chanas Ranch do not object to testimony based on Mr. Abell’s personal

observations regarding ranch operations, land use, or matters within ordinary landowner

experience. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Reliance Ranches and Chanas Ranch object to various

portions of the direct testimony of Mr. Samuel HV Abell (“Mr. Abell”) as improper lay witness

testimony since he is not an expert witness. Additionally, certain testimony and exhibits listed as

“Figures” in Mr. Abell’s direct testimony lack foundation and are not properly authenticated, lack

direct knowledge, and/or call for speculation. These portions are detailed in Section III.

    A. Lack of Personal Knowledge

    Under Tex. R. Evid. 602, a witness may not testify to a matter “unless evidence is introduced

sufficient to support a finding that the witness has personal knowledge of the matter.” Mr. Abell

offers testimony, including Figures 1-1 through 1-16, about which he lacks personal knowledge.

He presented no evidence or testimony to show that he created, or even has personal knowledge

of, the facts, data, and information contained in some testimony and in his attached Figures 1-1

through 1-16. These specific items are addressed in the charts below.

    B. Inappropriate Opinion Testimony

    Mr. Abell is not an expert under Tex. Rules of Evid. 701. A non-expert witness may only

provide testimony in the form of opinion when it is limited to one “rationally based on the witness's

perception”. When a witness offers an opinion as an expert, it must come from a witness who is

“qualified as an expert by knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education.” Mr. Abell has not

been designated as an expert in any field, and no facts or qualifications have been provided to

show that he has any specialized knowledge, training, skill, or experience related to any particular

RELIANCE RANCHES, LLC AND CHANAS RANCH, LLC’S OBJECTIONS TO AND MOTION TO STRIKE
PORTIONS OF SAMUEL HV ABELL ON BEHALF OF ABELL RANCHES, LTD.’S DIRECT TESTIMONY

(493,408)                                                                                    PAGE 2 OF 8
 subject matter. Nothing in Mr. Abell’s direct testimony identifies him as an expert, or that he has

any specialized training, skill, experience, education, or knowledge to provide an expert opinion

testimony related to 1) archeology, 2) hydrology, 3) ecology, or 4) geology. Accordingly, in some

of the testimony offered by Mr. Abell, he makes an opinion and statements about facts and data he

has no personal knowledge of and about which he is not an expert. His testimony exceeds

permissible lay opinion because it relies on specialized scientific, geological, archaeological,

hydrological, or ecological knowledge.

    C. Lack of Authentication for Figures 1-1 Through 1-16

    Evidence must be properly authenticated before it is admitted. A witness offering evidence,

such as exhibits, must satisfy this requirement by authenticating and identifying the item of

evidence. The witness “must produce evidence sufficient to support a finding that the item is what

the proponent claims it is.” Tex. R. Evid. 901. Mr. Abell has failed to satisfy this requirement for

Figures 1-1 through 1-16; he does not provide any evidence that any of these exhibits are what

they purport to be. Mr. Abell does not produce any evidence or offer any testimony that these

exhibits are true and accurate or that they have not been altered in any way. He does not present

any testimony on who prepared them and when, or if they were prepared based on that unknown

person’s (or group of people’s) own observation and knowledge. Furthermore, there is nothing in

his testimony to show that Figures 1-1 through 1-16 are self-authenticating as allowed under Tex

R. Evid. 902.
